name: Macro-Regime-Armed Crypto Trend (risk-on + non-extreme VIX gate, not trend-alone)
rationale: THESIS: Plain crypto trend/momentum is exhausted because it fires in every tape — including the chop and the risk-off bleed where it loses. The orthogonal structure is the GATE, not the trend: macro_regime (FRED curve+real-rates+liquidity composite, next-day available, BOUNDED 0-100-ish) and a non-extreme vix_level (BOUNDED) together define a 'risk premia are being paid' state. Documented macro->crypto coupling (Coinbase Institutional / S&P Global on crypto's regime-dependent equity-beta; Adler 'Bitcoin vs Macro Risk Score' = a DXY+10Y+VIX composite that overrides on-chain structure in risk-off) shows crypto co-moves with growth-equity beta in stress and de-risks when the macro tide goes out. We only take the long-only spot trend WHEN the macro window is open AND vol is non-extreme. This is below hedge-fund capacity (8 spot majors, daily, long-only, no leverage/shorts) and they run the fast leveraged perps version instead, so the slow daily regime-gated edge is left on the table. DISCONFIRMER: run the IDENTICAL ret_Nd>0 trend rule with the macro_regime+vix gate REMOVED (trend-alone). If gated and ungated produce statistically indistinguishable deflated-Sharpe, the regime gate carries no orthogonal info and the 'edge' is just already-exhausted momentum. The gate must add risk-adjusted return NET of the extra fees from missed-window exits.
catalyst: Macro regime turning risk-on (FRED curve/rates/liquidity composite rises above its fitted level) while implied vol stays non-extreme (vix below a fitted complacency/normal ceiling) and price trend is already up — the macro window opens and arms a trend that would otherwise also fire in losing risk-off tapes.
